title: MoS2 Contact Resistance Literature Outlier Investigation

case_studies.full_title: Phase-engineered low-resistance contacts to monolayer 2D semiconductors
case_studies.fabrication_process: Chemical phase transition via n-butyl lithium immersion converting 2H semiconducting MoS2 into metallic 1T phase
case_studies.extraction_method: Transfer Length Method (TLM) with varied contact spacings (0.5 - 5 um)
case_studies.characterization_environment: Room temperature ambient and vacuum probe station
case_studies.physical_root_cause: The 1T metallic phase homojunction eliminates the van der Waals tunnel barrier entirely, providing an atomically seamless covalent transition with near-unity carrier transmission. Standard regularized models predict Rc ~ 616 Ohm*um, but the seamless atomic transition achieves 240 Ohm*um, resulting in a negative residual (-0.41 dex, model overprediction).
case_studies.discrepancy_classification: Uncaptured atomic interface physics (covalent 2D homojunction vs 3D/2D heterojunction)

case_studies.full_title: Approaching the Schottky-Mott limit in van der Waals metal-semiconductor junctions
case_studies.fabrication_process: Mechanical transfer of pre-fabricated, ultra-flat Pt contact stripes onto monolayer MoS2 without high-energy evaporation damage
case_studies.contact_geometry: Top-contact pristine van der Waals interface
case_studies.extraction_method: Four-probe Transfer Length Method (TLM) as a function of temperature (77K - 300K) and gate bias
case_studies.physical_root_cause: Pt has a very high work function (~5.65 eV). In unpinned vdW junctions, this induces a massive electron Schottky barrier (Phi_B ~ 1.38 eV), driving the contact into extreme thermionic suppression. The model predicted 26.0 kOhm*um, but the measured resistance reached 65.0 kOhm*um (+0.40 dex underprediction). The discrepancy stems from high-field barrier lowering saturation and heavy effective mass of hole carriers.
case_studies.recommended_feature_enrichment: Non-linear barrier transmission term: exp(q*Phi_B / k_B*T)

case_studies.full_title: Defect-dominated doping and contact resistance in MoS2
case_studies.fabrication_process: Direct thermal evaporation of Pd onto mechanically exfoliated MoS2 flakes without chemical passivation
case_studies.extraction_method: In-situ X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) coupled with 2-terminal/TLM electrical transport
case_studies.characterization_environment: Ultra-High Vacuum (UHV, ~10^-10 Torr) and ambient re-exposure
case_studies.physical_root_cause: Evaporating high-melting-point Pd directly onto unpassivated MoS2 generates substantial sulfur vacancy defect clusters. These mid-gap defects pin the Fermi level rigidly near 0.35 eV below the conduction band and create high localized scattering centers. The model predicted 5.0 kOhm*um based on ideal Pd work function, whereas experimental defect generation degraded Rc to 12.0 kOhm*um (+0.38 dex underprediction).
